paragraphs: Here's what I see in this passage, friend. Solomon, king of Israel, has spent twenty years building two houses, the house of the LORD and his royal palace, and then the text just keeps listing his projects: cities, store cities, terraces, a fleet, tons of gold (1 Kings 9:10, 15-19, 28). Big, impressive, busy. But the Bible doesn't pile up all this greatness to make us gasp at a building schedule.

Look at the cracks, though. Hiram is not pleased with the twenty towns, and he asks, "What are these towns you have given me, my brother?" (1 Kings 9:12-13). Solomon also put the people still in the land to forced labor, but he did not consign any Israelites to slavery (1 Kings 9:21-22). I think this is a heavy part. Even in a shining reign, the account shows a king whose power touches a lot of people, and not every one of them is smiling.

So here's what I take home, baker. Big results don't tell the whole story, and the Bible isn't afraid to show us both the gold and the cost. Ask yourself what your own busy season costs the people around you, and whether the folks who help you are being treated like "brother" or like a tool. And one more thing: Solomon completed the temple, but the story isn't over. The Bible keeps telling it, so keep reading.
